trigger: raising the PR with no changelog.d fragment while amending a merge rule the shipped changelog already published to customers
summary: REVERSES the earlier exemption ruling. Gates 1-2 and this run's own docs-writer ruled the change exempt because reason/provenance never crosses the wire. That tests the wrong thing: changelog.d/README rule 3's bar is 'if an operator or agent would notice'. The parent PR #3258's fragment (20260817-wave2-discovery-native-arp-icmp.changed.md) explicitly PUBLISHED this merge rule - 'multiple independent degrade conditions in a single scan are now merged by severity onto that reason, rather than the last one silently overwriting an earlier, more actionable one'. This change amends that published rule, so a customer who read the shipped changelog now holds a stale model. Verified by reading the parent fragment and the README rule directly.
classification_rationale: A required doc (closed-list item 3, changelog fragment) is missing for a change that amends a previously published operator-facing claim. Absence is a truth finding, never capped at NICE.

trigger: reading the tie-break doc comment's attribution of the ARP pair to the sweep deadline
summary: Comment attributed the ARP pair's scan:timeout to the probe-loop deadline, which is near-unreachable in practice (its budget ceiling is well under kScanTimeoutSeconds); the timeout that actually reaches worst_of is the hostname loop's.
classification_rationale: A concrete attribution the code's own constants falsify.
fixed_ref: comment no longer names Step 4 and adds an explicit note on which deadline actually fires

trigger: a refactor moving do_scan_subnet's ICMP-session check above the ARP read, or the DNS degrade past the deadline check
summary: The fix's correctness rests on do_scan_subnet's accumulation order, which nothing pinned. Tests exercised worst_of with hand-built orders only, so a reordering refactor would silently re-break #3253 with every regression test green.
classification_rationale: Missing coverage of the ordering assumption the fix depends on; bounded blast radius, so SHOULD not a floor.
fixed_ref: new TEST_CASE 'the fold is order-dependent - three-way outcomes are pinned, not assumed' documents the real accumulation order and the concrete non-transitivity case

summary: Comment said the predicate accepts a row with 'a full 6-byte Ethernet MAC'; the code accepts phys_len >= 6, so 8-byte FireWire and 20-byte IPoIB addresses also pass.
classification_rationale: Stated contract is narrower than the code's actual accept set.
fixed_ref: comment now states 'at least a full 6-byte physical address', explains the >= vs == choice, and records the three-leg divergence as deliberately unconverged

trigger: a scan hitting three CONSTRAINED conditions, e.g. macOS {arp:table_truncated, icmp:transmit_blocked, scan:timeout} in do_scan_subnet's fixed accumulation order
summary: worst_of is a PAIRWISE fold and the named-pair tie-break is NOT transitive, so an unrelated third condition can change which true reason is reported. Reporter derived I3/HIGH; IMPACT corrected to I8 on evidence, NOT on judgment: the reported reason is always a TRUE statement about the scan (nothing wrong is presented as correct), and the caller CAN tell what else happened because every degrade condition writes its own status|warning line unconditionally BEFORE the merge (verified at discovery_plugin.cpp:542/573/587/630/702/719) and those lines reach the server in the command output stream. The single arbitrated reason additionally never crosses the wire at all - agents/core/src/agent.cpp:3095 is its only consumer, an spdlog::info. The reporter itself recorded that on this reduced blast radius the finding lands at MEDIUM, so it does not gate under its own alternative reading either. Also raised as ENT-3 by enterprise-readiness at INFO. Residual design question is real and is being filed.
classification_rationale: Valid design observation; the disagreement was over IMPACT class, resolved on the observable evidence above rather than by lowering a band. Recorded at both the reporter's native label and the corrected derivation.

trigger: ARP read fails AND the sweep hits its deadline in one scan
summary: arp:read_failed and icmp:socket_error are UNAVAILABLE severity so they dominate scan:timeout outright - no tie, tie-break never consulted - and their message text asserts a complete other half ('reporting ICMP-discovered hosts only') that a timeout may have truncated. PRE-EXISTING: the severity ladder and both message strings predate this branch and are untouched by it; this diff only makes the tension legible by codifying the opposite principle nearby. IMPACT corrected from the reporter's I3 to I8 for the same evidence as UP-1 (every condition still writes its own warning line; the arbitrated reason is log-only).
classification_rationale: A pre-existing message-accuracy issue surfaced, not introduced, by this change.

trigger: icmp:transmit_blocked or icmp:ping_group_range accumulating before the hostname loop's scan:timeout
summary: A third and fourth same-shape tie remain on earliest-wins: the two icmp:* reasons each accumulate before the hostname-loop scan:timeout. Deliberately NOT closed in this round - enterprise-readiness argued persuasively that an ICMP half that could not run AT ALL is more actionable than a deadline, so preferring the icmp reason is defensible and this is a genuine semantic question rather than the same bug. Both directions are pinned by CHECK_FALSE in the truth table, so the exclusion is regression-proof rather than silent, and the rationale is now recorded in the doc comment. Raised independently by happy-path, unhappy-path (UP-2) and enterprise-readiness (ENT-3).
classification_rationale: A scope decision with a recorded rationale, not an oversight.

trigger: a mixed-OS fleet scanning a subnet with a non-Ethernet or >6-byte-hwaddr neighbour
summary: The three ARP legs disagree on three axes, not one: Windows accepts phys_len >= 6 (macOS requires exactly 6, Linux filters hwtype == 0x1); Windows and macOS accept an all-zero MAC that Linux drops; neither Windows nor macOS filters hardware type. A 20-byte IPoIB neighbour is accepted on Windows and format_mac48 renders its first 6 bytes as a plausible MAC-48. E6 applies and dominates: this diff changed no accept/reject decision on any leg - the extraction is byte-faithful and behaviour is identical to shipped dev - so the wrong outcome is not newly reachable. Raised independently by plugin-developer, cross-platform, consistency-auditor and enterprise-readiness; consistency-auditor's is the broadest characterisation and is the one recorded.
classification_rationale: A real cross-leg semantic divergence, surfaced rather than introduced; the newly-pure predicate is now the natural convergence point.

summary: The degrade reason this whole change arbitrates never leaves the endpoint - to_proto_result_status carries only the coarse enum - and there is no Prometheus counter for plugin degrade outcomes on either side. Both are pre-existing ABI4-seam properties this change merely touches; a per-reason counter is blocked on the reason reaching the wire first. Raised independently by sre and compliance-officer.
classification_rationale: An observability gap in the seam, not a required-doc absence and not introduced here.

Corrected from 'wording' per Gate 8 security-guardian: a structural defence-in-depth suggestion is not a wording observation. Band and disposition unchanged; this supersession neither weakens the gate nor the band.

adjudicated_by: security-guardian (Gate 8 re-review, pass 2) — NOT the author of the reviewed commits, and not the agent that raised the finding
adjudication_rationale: Separation in force: the de-escalation rule's, for an IMPACT restatement that lowers the band from the reporter's native HIGH. Gate 8 security-guardian was asked to judge whether the I3->I8 correction was honest or a band-lowering, and independently re-verified BOTH load-bearing facts before ruling it honest: (1) the arbitrated reason is passed as provenance and its sole consumer is the spdlog::info at agent.cpp:3095 - no result_reason field exists anywhere off the endpoint; (2) every degrade condition writes its own status|warning line before the merge (verified at 542/573/587/630/702/719). I3 requires 'the caller cannot tell', which is false on that evidence. The reporter's native HIGH is retained on the raising row, so nothing is erased. CAVEAT RECORDED HONESTLY: per the skill's own rule a subagent of the authoring session is not truly independent, so this is an audit trail rather than a verified control, and it is flagged to the operator for review rather than treated as settled.

schema_note: gate-8 finding on the fix diff
trigger: reading the order-dependence TEST_CASE's comment and believing it guards do_scan_subnet's accumulation order
summary: The order-pinning test added in pass 1 (itself in response to UP-8) over-claimed: its comment said a reordering of do_scan_subnet would flip it, which is false - the test hardcodes its own fold order and never references do_scan_subnet. Two of its three CHECKs also duplicated assertions already present in the file. Called out as 'partly theatre', correctly.
classification_rationale: A test comment asserting a guarantee the test does not provide is the false-assurance shape, even though the assertions themselves are true.
fixed_ref: test renamed to name what it actually pins (worst_of's non-transitivity), the false reordering claim replaced with an explicit statement that NO test observes the accumulation order and why, and the duplicated CHECK removed

summary: The order-dependence test relied on a severity tie without asserting one, so a reclassification would make it pass via the severity branch for the wrong reason.
classification_rationale: Missing precondition that keeps the test observing what it claims.

trigger: reading the new changelog fragment's causal sentence against do_scan_subnet's accumulation order
summary: The fragment reintroduced, in operator-facing text, the exact universal claim CON-2 had just removed from the code comment - that the ARP read and reverse-DNS resolution ALWAYS run before the scan deadline. ARP always does; reverse-DNS does not.
classification_rationale: A false causal claim in a customer-facing artefact; the outcome claims around it were verified correct.

trigger: reading the tie-break comment's parenthetical about the probe-loop-before-DNS ordering
summary: The pass-1 correction to CON-2 was itself imprecise: it presented probe-loop-timeout-before-DNS-degrade as a live ordering. Positionally true, but the two cannot co-occur - if the probe loop consumed the budget, the hostname loop's deadline check breaks on iteration 1 so hostname_degraded stays 0. A correction that is itself inaccurate is exactly the fix-round defect Gate 8 exists to catch.
classification_rationale: Comment described a reachable path that is unreachable.
fixed_ref: parenthetical now states the two cannot co-occur and why, retaining the harmless-either-way note
